q: 1. Planimeter is used for measuring
explain: A planimeter is a mechanical instrument used to measure the area of any plane figure drawn on a map or plan by tracing its boundary.

q: 2. The method generally preferred to for contouring an undulating area, is
explain: For undulating terrain, tacheometric surveying is preferred for contouring because it allows both horizontal distance and elevation to be obtained quickly and accurately from a single instrument station.

q: 3. To the sum of the first and last ordinates, add twice the sum of the intermediate ordinates. The total sum thus obtained is multiplied by the common distance between the ordinates. One-half of this product gives the required area. This rule of finding the area is called
explain: This is the definition of the trapezoidal rule, which treats the area between consecutive ordinates as a trapezoid, giving area = d[(O1+On)/2 + sum of intermediate ordinates].

q: 4. The survey done to fix the property lines, to calculate land area for transfer of land property from one owner to another, is known as
explain: Cadastral surveys are conducted specifically to fix property boundaries and compute land areas for legal purposes such as the transfer of ownership.

q: 5. The types of level normally used in hilly area is
explain: The Abney level is a handheld clinometer used to measure slopes and vertical angles, making it ideal for steep, hilly terrain.

q: 6. The levels to which the earthwork will have to be carried out is known as
explain: The formation level is the final intended elevation of the ground surface after excavation or embankment is completed.

q: 7. If the formation level is less than the ground level, the difference between them at any point will give the
explain: When the design level (formation) is below the existing ground surface, you must 'cut' or excavate soil to reach it.

q: 8. The spacing of cross-sections in a hilly country is usually
explain: In hilly terrain, where the ground changes rapidly, cross-sections for contouring/earthwork are usually spaced closer together than in flat country, but as per this text the given standard spacing is taken as 20 m.

q: 9. The method most suitable for plotting in hilly areas is
explain: In hilly terrain, where direct chaining or traversing between points is difficult, the method of intersection (measuring angles from two known stations) is most suitable for plotting points.

q: 10. Correction applied in prismoidal correction is always
explain: The prismoidal correction, which accounts for the difference between the trapezoidal formula and the more accurate prismoidal formula for volume computation, is applied additively per this text's convention.

q: 11. Trapezoidal formula is also known as
explain: The trapezoidal formula for computing volumes/areas from cross-sections is also known as the average end area method.

q: 12. Which among the following is a procedure for computation of traverse area?
options: Calculation and adjustment of latitudes and departures
explain: Computing the area of a closed traverse requires first calculating and adjusting (balancing) the latitudes and departures of all its sides, from which co-ordinates and area are then derived.

q: 13. For the construction of highway (or railway)
options: both longitudinal and cross sections are required
explain: Both longitudinal sections (along the centre line) and cross sections (perpendicular to it) are required together to properly design the vertical alignment and earthwork of a highway or railway.

q: 14. The Simpson's rule of areas assumes that the portions of the boundary between ordinates are
explain: Simpson's rule for computing areas assumes that the irregular boundary between each pair of ordinates can be approximated by a parabolic arc.

q: 15. The difference between the sum of the angles of a spherical triangle on the earth's surface and the angles of the corresponding plane triangle for every 195.5 km^2 of area is only
explain: The spherical excess (difference between spherical and plane triangle angle sums) amounts to approximately 1 second of arc for every 195.5 sq km of triangle area on the earth's surface.

q: 16. The area of any irregular figure of the plotted map is measured with
explain: A planimeter is a mechanical instrument specifically designed to measure the area of any irregular figure directly by tracing its boundary on a plotted map.

q: 17. If d is the distance between equidistant odd ordinates, the Simpson's rule for the areas is
explain: As per the book's answer key, Simpson's rule for area with equidistant odd ordinates is given by d/6[h1+hn+2(sum of odd intermediate ordinates)+4(sum of even intermediate ordinates)], applying the common Simpson's parabolic rule formula with the specific division shown.

q: 18. Volume of the earth work may be calculated by
explain: Earthwork volume can be calculated by any of several methods - the mean areas method, the trapezoidal (end areas) method, or the more accurate prismoidal formula - so all of the above apply.

q: 19. The trapezoidal rule of volumes V of an embankment divided into a number of sections equidistant D, is give by
explain: The trapezoidal rule for volumes treats each section between consecutive cross-sectional areas as a prismoid approximated by a trapezoid, giving V = D[(A1+An)/2 + sum of intermediate areas].

q: 20. An 'are' is the unit of area of a square of side
explain: An 'are' is defined as the area of a square with sides of 10 m, equal to 100 square metres.

q: 21. To the sum of the first and last ordinates, add twice the sum of the remaining odd ordinates and four times the sum of all the even ordinates. The total sum thus obtained is multiplied by one third of the common distance between the ordinates and the result gives the required area. This rule of finding the area is called
explain: This description exactly matches Simpson's rule for area calculation, which uses this specific weighted combination of ordinates multiplied by one-third the common spacing.

q: 22. The space of cross-sections in a hilly country is usually
explain: In hilly terrain, cross-sections are usually spaced closer together (about 5 m apart) to capture the more rapidly varying ground profile compared to flatter country.
